## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ambasakkarapetavatthu* (Pv 36) is a narrative poem in the *Mahāvagga* of the *Petavatthu* (PTS pp. 45–57) [Marino 2017]. Framed around the central question of how one escapes the path leading to hell, the narrative depicts the titular ruler, King Ambasakkhara, alongside a *yakkha-peta* (yakṣa ghost) witnessing the prolonged public torture of a criminal who is bound or impaled on a stake [Marino 2017]. Prompted by the criminal's agony and dread of hellish torment, the ghost warns the king that impalement on a stake is vastly preferable to the terrors of hell, cautioning Ambasakkhara that he too remains at risk of such an excruciating fate [Marino 2017].
